body.name: Censoring-adjusted cross-fitted margin and inversion procedure
body.construction:
For a bounded terminal full-history functional \(F\) in arm \(a\), put \(\theta_{a,F}=\mathsf E\{F(\mathcal H_K^a)\}\), \(g_a=\mathsf P(R=a)\), and
\[
 g_\ell^a(h)=\mathsf P(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,
 D_{\ell-1}^a=0,\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h),
 \qquad
 \bar G_\ell^a=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}g_j^a(\mathcal H_{j-1}^a).
\]
Set \(Q_{K,F}^a=F\).  Backwards over supported alive histories, set
\[
 Q_{\ell-1,F}^a(h)=
 \mathsf E\{Q_{\ell,F}^a(\mathcal H_\ell^a)
       \mid \mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h\},
\]
and on a dead history use the deterministic absorbing completion.  Define
\[
 \Psi_{a,F}(O)=
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R=a\}}{g_a}\left[Q_{0,F}^a(\mathcal H_0^a)+
 \sum_{\ell=1}^{K}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{C\ge\ell,D_{\ell-1}^a=0\}}{\bar G_\ell^a}
 \{Q_{\ell,F}^a(\mathcal H_\ell^a)-Q_{\ell-1,F}^a(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a)\}\right],
 \qquad
 \varphi_{a,F}=\Psi_{a,F}-\theta_{a,F}.                    \tag{1}
\]
Use the terminal cell indicators
\[
 F_{bt}^1=\mathbf 1\{S_k^1=1,B=b,T=t\},\qquad
 F_w^0=\mathbf 1\{S_k^0=1,\min\{Z,H\}=w\},\qquad
 F_S^0=\mathbf 1\{S_k^0=1\}.                              \tag{2}
\]
Then \(r_{bt}=\theta_{1,F_{bt}^1}\), \(\nu_w=\theta_{0,F_w^0}\), \(\sigma_0=\theta_{0,F_S^0}\), \(q_w=\nu_w/\sigma_0\), and the ratio influence function is
\[
 \varphi_{q_w}=\frac{\varphi_{0,F_w^0}-q_w\varphi_{0,F_S^0}}{\sigma_0}. \tag{3}
\]
The procedure \(\mathfrak I\) uses a fixed number of folds.  On each validation fold it evaluates (1) with backward regressions and censoring hazards fitted only on the complementary training folds, with regressions clipped to \([0,1]\) and hazards clipped to \([\varepsilon/2,1]\), and averages the resulting scores.  For \(q_w\), it divides the cross-fitted numerator estimate by the maximum of the corresponding survival-denominator estimate and \(\varepsilon/2\).  Let \(\widehat\vartheta_n^{\mathrm{raw}}\) collect these estimates of \(((r_{bt}),(q_w))\), and let \(\widetilde\vartheta_n\) be a sup-norm projection onto the compact set of Hall-feasible margin pairs having intensive-survivor mass at least \(\varepsilon/2\).  With \(d=(H+1)^2+(H+1)\) and any valid uniform bound \(C_{K,\varepsilon}\) on the influence-function coordinates, it takes the simultaneous Bonferroni--Chebyshev rectangle centered at \(\widetilde\vartheta_n\) with coordinate half-width
\[
 \frac{2\{C_{K,\varepsilon}\sqrt{d/\alpha}+1\}}{\sqrt n},              \tag{4}
\]
clipped to \([0,1]\).  The endpoints in (4) define \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\), which is then inverted through \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{n,\alpha}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}\).  This definition introduces no quantitative restriction into \(\mathfrak M_H\); its positive rate guarantee is conditional on \(\operatorname{QIR}_{H,K,\varepsilon}\).
